Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 23 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal & expansion: flexible bandwidth credits + co-term pivot

Hi Alicia / Mark,

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday — great context on Juniper's Q3 spike and downstream risk buckets. To make procurement easier while keeping your ops predictable, I've sketched two pragmatic options the team can evaluate quickly. Attached is a simple model so you can flip assumptions.

High-level (current state):
- Contract mid-term increase of ~40% in consumption projected for next 12 months (mainly embeddings + embedding-based rerank).
- Current term: co-term ends 2029-02-15.

Option A — Flexible band + incremental credits (preferred for ops):
- Add a temporary +45% "burst band" on top of committed units for Q3–Q4.
- One-time credit equal to 10% of next 3 months' token spend (applied as invoice credit).
- Co-term: keep existing term, no change.
- Billing: monthly; no upfront change.

Option B — Co-term pivot + price smoothing (preferred for procurement/legal):
- Annualize the uplift and move to a co-term extension to 2030-02-15.
- Provide a 5% rebate on year 2 invoices in exchange for the extended co-term.
- Include a capped burst allowance with overage applied at standard pay-as-you-go rates.

Questions for you: which option maps closer to procurement's appetite? If procurement prefers Option B I can pull in Kimberly (renewals) and legal to draft an amendment. If ops prefers Option A we can sign a one-page amendment and enable the burst band within 48–72 hours.

Attachments: pricing-model-v3.xlsx (token classes, sample invoice sim).

Next steps: let me know a preferred option and whether procurement needs a single POC for legal redlines or the full SOW. Happy to jump on a short call tomorrow.

Best,
Sofia
